notes.text: Requires the WordPress Manager cPanel plugin, available from WordPress Manager 3.0. The site argument, where present, is the caller-selected WordPress URL without a protocol prefix and may contain a path. No site value is inferred. The client does not poll SSE paths or fetch archive URLs.

All documented response object fields are optional. Omission is distinct from explicit null, empty lists and zero flags. Integer flags remain 0|1 without string or boolean normalization. This method is explicitly read-only in the pinned source and uses GET.

The pinned full examples place any_running, sites and last_outcome directly under data; the formal schema places the same fields under optional items. Both placements are preserved in one object, including when both are present. Their fields remain optional and retain zero flags, explicit documented null and empty collections. These shapes are supported by pinned documentation and offline replay; no successful live WordPress response was observed.

sites preserves the known list row shape with optional nullable-string id and string site/type fields, plus the formal unstructured object alternative, which has only been documented as empty. No populated keyed-record schema is inferred. The source describes restore-process IDs as unimplemented/null-only while the formal id schema is nullable string. last_outcome.error is nullable string; status remains text and have_outcome is a 0|1 integer flag. any_running=0 alone does not establish completed restoration.

On the reviewed cPanel 11.138.0.19 installation, this method failed through both direct and bridged UAPI because Cpanel/API/WordPressRestore.pm was missing. The installed cpanel-wpx-plugin did not provide a usable module. This is an installation-specific capability failure; no successful payload or route incompatibility was established.

Preserve both placements together in one object with optional fields, avoiding first-match optional-object union loss. RestoreInProgress supplies the known optional nullable-string id and string site/type list row; RestoreNotInProgress formally declares an unstructured object sites. Cleans temporary system resources after restoration. The data is an integer 0|1 flag, with 0 meaning unsuccessful cleanup. It is distinct from the UAPI envelope status. Null and absent payloads are mismatches; cleanup is not a promise to undo restored files or to delete archives.

backupPath is the path to an existing server-side backup archive, forwarded unchanged as backup_path, not a local file upload. Starts restoration of the selected site and returns an optional restore_id. The source declares no rollback. Restoration changes site state and its process ID alone does not establish completion.
